'''Victor Lamar Law Jr.''' (born December 19, 1995) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Ryukyu Golden Kings]] of the Japanese [[B.League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball|Northwestern Wildcats]].

== High school career ==
Law was born in [[Chicago]], Illinois<ref>{{Cite web |title=#23 Vic Law |url=http://stats.washingtonpost.com/nba/playerstats.asp?id=6277&team=19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210127083206/http://stats.washingtonpost.com/nba/playerstats.asp?id=6277&team=19 |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 27, 2021 |access-date=January 13, 2020 |website=[[washingtonpost.com]]}}</ref> and attended [[St. Rita of Cascia High School]]. In his sophomore year at St. Rita he was selected in the Catholic League All-Conference team; in his junior year he averaged 14.5 points and 9.5 rebounds, and was selected in the All-State third team. As a high school senior Law was included in the top 100 players in the nation by [[ESPN]] (which ranked him 66th), [[Scout.com]] (70th), [[247Sports.com]] (89th) and [[Rivals.com]] (86th). He received interest from several [[NCAA Division I|Division I]] colleges, and was offered scholarships by [[Bradley Braves men's basketball|Bradley]], [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]], [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado]], [[Harvard Crimson men's basketball|Harvard]], [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence]] and [[Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball|Northwestern]], among others; he committed to Northwestern on July 4, 2013<ref>{{Cite web |title=Victor Law |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/125694 |access-date=January 13, 2020 |website=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref> and signed on November 13 of the same year.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://247sports.com/Player/Vic-Law-28349/high-school-46937/|title=Vic Law|website=[[247Sports.com]]|access-date=January 13, 2020}}</ref>

==College career==
[[File: 20170301 NW-UM Vic Law in the halfcourt.jpg|thumb|150px|left|Law at Northwestern in 2017]]
He joined the Northwestern Wildcats in 2014 after his senior year of high school.<ref>{{cite web|first=Michael|last=Osipoff|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/suburbs/post-tribune/sports/ct-sta-spt-mens-basketball-st-rita-vic-law-charles-matthews-st-1031-story.html|title=All about St. Rita: Northwestern's Vic Law, Michigan's Charles Matthews maintain connection|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|date=October 30, 2018|access-date=January 12, 2020}}</ref> He had a strong freshman season, starting 19 games as a freshman and averaging 7.0 points and 4.8 rebounds per game. Law shot 44.2% from behind the arc, which was fifth best in the [[Big Ten Conference]]. He tore a labrum in the summer of 2015 and missed the [[2015–16 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2015–16 season]] after undergoing shoulder surgery.<ref>{{cite web|last=Chavez|first=Christopher|title=Northwestern's Vic Law (torn labrum) to undergo surgery, out for season|url=https://www.si.com/college/2015/11/11/northwestern-basketball-vic-law-torn-labrum-surgery-out-year|date=November 11, 2015|publisher=[[Sports Illustrated]]|access-date=January 12, 2020}}</ref>

As a [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] sophomore, Law averaged 12.3 points, 5.8 rebounds and 1.8 assists per game.<ref name="greenstein"/> Law was a Big Ten All-Defensive Team selection in 2017. He helped Northwestern reach the [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] for the first time in the school's history.<ref>{{cite news |last=Duber |first=Vinnie |title=Can Vic Law be the biggest difference-maker and help Northwestern get to the Sweet Sixteen? |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/chicago/big-ten/can-vic-law-be-biggest-difference-maker-and-help-northwestern-get-sweet-sixteen |access-date=January 12, 2020 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=March 17, 2017}}</ref> During his junior season, he averaged 12.0 points and 5.8 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite news |title=Northwestern |url=https://madison.com/northwestern/article_39a2bdb6-e062-5b3d-b967-e116bce6c743.html |access-date=January 12, 2020 |work=Madison.com |date=November 6, 2018}}</ref> In March 2018, he underwent an unusual diaphragm surgery to address a deficiency in his lung capacity.<ref name="greenstein">{{cite news |last=Greenstein |first=Teddy |title=Northwestern hoping unusual surgery gives Vic Law a 2nd wind in his 5th season |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/ct-spt-northwestern-vic-law-surgery-20181012-story.html |access-date=January 12, 2020 |work=[[Chicago Tribune]] |date=October 12, 2018}}</ref> As a senior, Law started 30 games and averaged 15.0 points, 6.4 rebounds, 3.0 assists, and 1.03 blocks per game. He was named Academic All-Big Ten for the second year in a row. Law appeared in 125 career games in four seasons at Northwestern, averaging 11.5 points, 5.7 rebounds and 2.0 assists per game.<ref name=nba/>

==Professional career==

=== Lakeland Magic (2019–2020) ===
After going undrafted in the [[2019 NBA draft]], Law played for the [[Orlando Magic]] in the [[2019 NBA Summer League|NBA Summer League]] and joined them for training camp and preseason.<ref name="realgm">{{cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Vic-Law/Summary/52054|title=Vic Law|work=realgm.com|access-date=August 27, 2021}}</ref> He was allocated by Orlando to their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Lakeland Magic]].

=== Orlando Magic (2020) ===
On January 11, 2020, Law signed a [[two-way contract]] with Orlando. Under the terms of the deal, he split time between Orlando and Lakeland.<ref name="nba">{{cite web |last=Cohen |first=Josh |date=January 11, 2020 |title=Magic Sign Magette to 10-Day Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/magic-sign-magette-10-day-contract-20200111 |access-date=January 12, 2020 |work=NBA.com}}</ref> Law was named to the All-NBA G League Third Team.<ref>{{cite web |title=Johnson, Magette and Law Named to All-NBA G League Teams |url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/johnson-magette-and-law-named-to-all-nba-g-league-teams/n-5625789 |website=Our Sports Central |access-date=June 28, 2020 |date=June 26, 2020}}</ref> In 33 games for Lakeland during the 2019–20 season, he averaged 19.7 points, 8.1 rebounds and 2.7 assist per game.<ref name="realgm"/> He also played in eight NBA regular season games and one playoff game with Orlando.<ref name="realgm"/>

=== Brisbane Bullets (2020–2021) ===
On December 4, 2020, Law signed with the [[Brisbane Bullets]] in Australia for the [[2020–21 NBL season]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Bullets Sign NBA Talent Vic Law |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/bullets-sign-nba-talent-vic-law |website=NBL.com.au |access-date=December 4, 2020 |date=December 4, 2020}}</ref> He was ruled out for the rest of the season on April 8, 2021, due to a torn tendon in his ankle that required surgery.<ref>{{cite web |title=Vic Law Ruled Out of NBL21 with Injury |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/vic-law-ruled-out-of-nbl21-with-injury |website=NBL.com.au |access-date=April 8, 2021 |date=April 8, 2021}}</ref>

For the [[2021 NBA Summer League]], Law played for the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref name="realgm"/>

=== Chiba Jets Funabashi (2022–present) ===
Law joined the [[Utah Jazz]] for the [[2022 NBA Summer League]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Utah Jazz 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612762/jazz |access-date=July 5, 2022 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> and then moved to Japan to play for the [[Chiba Jets Funabashi]] in the 2022–23 [[B.League]] season.<ref>{{cite web |date=July 21, 2022 |title=#4 ヴィック・ロー選手 2022-23シーズン選手契約基本合意（新規）のお知らせ |url=https://chibajets.jp/news/detail/id=20891 |access-date=January 29, 2023 |work=chibajets.jp |language=ja}}</ref>
